name: Module 6: the extraction UNIT CELL - metabolome + proteome from one extraction of adherent cells (demo scale, one lane pattern)
description: THE EXTRACTION UNIT CELL, AT DEMO SCALE. This chip is the proven unit cell for ONE culture lane: the geometry and the chemistry that get a metabolome AND a proteome out of adherent cells in one extraction. chip/module1_target_v1.json TILES THIS PATTERN at the ANSI/SLAS target footprint, where each lane carries replicated fields and some fields are quenched in place for metabolome + proteome while other fields in the SAME lane are dissociated for the single-cell transcriptome - which is what finally makes 'multi-omic from one sample' true. This chip is NOT a competing culture chip and no culture scale-up belongs in it: it cultures its own cells here only because a unit cell has to be testable on its own, and at target scale the cells arrive from the module 1 lanes. Keep it standalone and self-consistent; put replication in the target chip. WHAT IT IS. Metabolome AND proteome from ONE cold acidified organic extraction of ADHERENT cells, in place on the chamber floor, before any encapsulation. 30 x 20 mm, ONE fluidic layer at ONE etch depth of 0.3 mm, resin print + hot emboss, geometry only from contracts/blocks.json (culture_chamber, centipede_channel). Three lanes (neurons, glia, astrocytes) that never share a wetted path: each lane is one culture field (1.2 x 8 x 0.3 mm, 2.88 uL), one inlet comb, one outlet comb, one inlet port and one outlet port. LANE VOLUMES ARE DATA NOW, NOT PROSE. The field sits in SERIES with its combs and port stubs, so the numbers that matter are per LANE, and all of them are derived in protocols/build_module6.py from this file plus contracts/: inlet stub 1.003 uL (a 800 um hole through 1 mm of lid, plus an ASSUMED 0.5 uL off-chip valve stub) + inlet comb 3.186 uL = 4.189 uL UPSTREAM of the field; 2.88 uL of FIELD; the same 4.189 uL DOWNSTREAM; 11.258 uL wetted per lane. A comb is its spine (path length x width x depth from the channel entry) plus its tooth band, and the tooth band is data too: 13 teeth of 0.2 x 1.5 mm because the tooth width is contracts/blocks.json min_open_channel_mm, the rib is min_wall_mm, the pitch is their sum, and the tooth LENGTH is the gap this file already states between the spine edge and the field edge. Nothing about the comb volume is a quoted figure any more. The chip_spec schema has no volume field for a channel, which is why the derivation lives in the builder and its result is written here. WHY THE LOAD WAS OVERFILLING, AND WHAT CHANGED. The hand-maintained protocol used to push one whole lane wetted volume (11.444 uL) and call it a LOAD into a 2.88 uL chamber - 3.97 chamber volumes, which tests/test_design_rules.py now fails. Reconciled by CAPPING THE LOAD AT WHAT THE CHAMBER HOLDS: the load is exactly one field volume, and the 4.189 uL of upstream dead volume the suspension has to cross first is its own PRIME step, named and costed. The alternative - inflating the chamber's volume_ul to the lane volume so the old load 'fitted' - would have made the chamber lie about its own box (1.2 x 8 x 0.3 mm really is 2.88 uL) and tools/validate.py checks exactly that. Capping also fixes something real: the suspension front now stops at the FAR FIELD EDGE, so the OUTLET comb is never filled with cells and the 'stray cells settle in the comb' risk is handled by the volume instead of by an adhesion coat that is still untested. Cell suspension spent per lane drops from 11.258 to 7.069 uL. WHY ADHERENT CELLS AND NOT CAPSULES. GelMA is gelatin, so it is itself protein, and proteomics on capsules would partly measure the capsule. The number this repo used to quote was wrong by about 4x, though, and it is worth having right: 30-45x assumed a SOLID 70 um sphere of gelatin. These are CORE-SHELL capsules with a liquid core, so only the shell is gelatin, and an ASSUMED 3 um shell is 24% of the capsule volume - about 2.1 ng of gelatin against 0.2-0.3 ng of cell protein, so roughly 7-11x, not 30-45x. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES INTACT: a 7-10x protein background that is itself a proteolytically-digestible protein still swamps the measurement, so extraction belongs on adherent cells. Native cytosolic protein could also leak out through the shell before the solvent denatures it (unmeasured). Extracting from adherent cells has no gelatin background, is published practice (direct cold solvent on adherent cells beat scrape-in-buffer 7x, Dettmer 2011 doi 10.1007/s00216-010-4425-x; one extraction giving proteins and metabolites, SIMPLEX, Coman 2016 doi 10.1074/mcp.M115.053702; supernatant for metabolites then the pellet digested for protein, Sapcariu 2014 doi 10.1016/j.mex.2014.07.002) and it removes the retention problem, because a 25 um weir gap cannot be printed at the 200 um in-plane floor. The single-cell transcriptome arm is unaffected and is a different sample path: on this demo chip it is module 4 on capsules (per-cell barcode made per capsule in its own oil droplet); at target scale it is the dissociated fields of the same lane. This chip is the bulk arm only. WHAT THE CITATIONS DO AND DO NOT SUPPORT. A biology audit found figures travelling further than their methods, so the limits are recorded here rather than in a footnote. (1) SIMPLEX and Sapcariu are cited for the PRINCIPLE - metabolites in the supernatant, protein in the pellet, one extraction - and for the cold soak time, NOT for proteome depth or CV equivalence. Sapcariu is a CHLORINATED-SOLVENT (Folch-type) biphasic partition, and this chip excludes chlorinated solvents because they attack PMMA and swell COC. (2) The usual chlorinated-free substitute is an ETHER-TYPE biphasic partition (the chemistry behind SIMPLEX), and it does not rescue the material argument here: ethers of that class craze acrylic, and contracts/materials.json says COC resists polar solvents, acids and bases well but is ATTACKED BY NON-POLAR HYDROCARBONS, which is the family the substitute belongs to. So swapping the chlorinated solvent for an ether moves the material risk rather than removing it, AND IT MATTERS THAT THIS CHIP IS COC AND NOT PMMA: the repo's 'test on a PMMA coupon first' line is about a different polymer. The way out is that our chemistry is neither - a SINGLE-PHASE acidified polar-organic precipitation with no partition solvent at all - so no biphasic method's depth or CV figures transfer and any such number is marked NOT TRANSFERABLE. COC compatibility with our actual quench and solubilisation reagents is still TODO in contracts/materials.json. (3) The '>90% membrane protein recovery after organic precipitation' figure is specific to COLD ACID resolubilisation. The protocol used to resolubilise in a generic denaturing buffer at 37 C, where a common chaotrope carbamylates peptides and blocks identification, so the chemistry did not match the citation. The step now runs at AMBIENT with a non-carbamylating denaturant class and the >90% number is NOT claimed. FLOW, PER LANE. Seed and culture the adherent cells in the field (cell-adhesion coat on the field floor only, masked off the combs: untested). Brief ice-cold volatile-buffer rinse (mandatory, and SHORT - see RINSE). Stop-flow cold acidified organic quench in place, using a generic organic quench solvent that excludes chlorinated solvents, cells lysed where they sit. Cold soak. Collect FRACTION 1 = METABOLOME out of the outlet; small peptides under about 10 kDa do not precipitate and land in this fraction, not the protein one. Flush, then resolubilise the precipitated protein left on the chamber floor at ambient. Collect FRACTION 2 = PROTEOME out of the SAME outlet at a later time. The protein is denatured by design: native complexes and enzyme activity are lost; bottom-up identification and quantification are not. Fraction 1 is neutralised the moment it is collected (the vial is pre-charged off chip), because acid plus organic is only safe for RNA and acid-labile metabolites briefly. COMBS (the quench-speed fix). The old 20 s figure came from sweeping solvent along the long axis. Here the field is fed and drained through INTERDIGITATED COMBS along its two long edges, each a centipede_channel (a spine with short side branches): an inlet comb on the left edge (spine 0.8 mm wide, 13 teeth of 0.2 x 1.5 mm at 0.6 mm pitch) and an outlet comb on the right edge with 13 teeth offset by half a pitch, so teeth alternate along the 8 mm edge. Teeth are 0.2 mm wide with 0.4 mm ribs, meeting the 0.4 mm wall floor exactly. The inlet port sits at the top end of the left spine and the outlet port at the bottom end of the right spine (Z layout), so every tooth pair sees about the same total path. Flow then crosses the field's SHORT dimension, 1.2 mm, not its 8 mm length, so displacement time no longer depends on chamber length. Per unit flow, sweeping the long axis would need about 44x the pressure (path squared) and 6.7x the floor shear. A resistor-network model of this lane (Hele-Shaw field plus rectangular-duct teeth and spines) gives 1.37e+10 Pa s/m3 and tooth flows from 0.61 to 2.02 of the mean (uneven; a wider spine evens it but adds extract volume). The quench floods 2 wetted volumes (22.516 uL) in about 1 s (1351 uL/min): 308 Pa across the lane plus about 3.7 kPa across 100 mm of 0.5 mm bore line, total well under 10 kPa. Do NOT freeze-quench with the Peltier: at 2-10 K/s it takes 6-30 s, slower than the flood. THE FLOOD IS NOT STOKES FLOW, AND SEVERAL ARGUMENTS ELSEWHERE ASSUME Re << 1. A physics audit recomputed it and the builder now derives it: at 1351 uL/min the feed line runs Re ~ 19 and the comb SPINE Re ~ 14, with an entrance length of about 0.36 mm in the spine, so the flood is an INERTIAL, ENTRANCE-EFFECT regime with real minor losses at each tooth branch. Only the teeth (Re ~ 2.4) and the field itself (Re ~ 1.8) are anywhere near creeping, and even they are not Re << 1. THE ~1 s QUENCH CLAIM ITSELF CHECKS OUT and is not weakened: 0.13 s convective sweep across the 1.2 mm field plus 0.18 s diffusion over a 12 um cell at the contract diffusivity (0.52 s if D is cut by the cold, more viscous solvent), so 0.31-0.65 s. What changes is the JUSTIFICATION: uniformity rests on TOOTH CONVECTION, not on creeping flow. RISK THAT FOLLOWS: the 0.4 mm ribs leave 0.3-0.6 mm dead zones behind them, and diffusion alone would take 326-1303 s to clear those (the audit put it at 450-1800 s with a lower D). Tooth convection is therefore LOAD-BEARING, not a nicety: if the teeth do not actually convect into the rib shadows, those cells are quenched hundreds of seconds late and their fast metabolites are fiction. Model only - no measurement. QUENCH SPEED, HONEST LIMIT, REVISITED AFTER THE RINSE FIX. With a quench of about 1 s you lose only the fastest roughly 10-15% of a panel. The rinse used to dominate that budget: the old file pushed 22.516 uL at the culture ceiling, which took 700 s, so EVERYTHING fast was invalid. At 18 s the verdict changes, but only partly. ATP/ADP, phosphocreatine, NAD(P)H and the phosphorylated glycolytic intermediates turn over in about 1 s; even at 4 C, where metabolism is slowed several-fold, an 18 s rinse is still many turnover times, so THE CAVEAT STANDS UNCHANGED: treat ATP/ADP and glycolytic intermediates as INVALID. Sizing the rinse from the exchange target rather than from 2 lane volumes took it from 23 s to 18 s, and the bare contract floor would be 13.7 s - none of those cross the ~1 s turnover, so no amount of tightening the rinse rescues the fastest pool; only moving the quench upstream of the rinse would, and that is not possible on this chemistry. TCA intermediates and amino acids turn over in tens of seconds to minutes, so at 18 s cold they move from 'provisional' to usable - that part of the caveat is lifted. Lipids were never at risk. SHEAR, AND THE CEILING THAT APPLIES. The 0.01 dyn/cm2 culture ceiling applies to steps with LIVING adherent cells that have to stay attached for days: prime, load and culture exchange. It is held on the field with 15% headroom and the hottest tooth region (2.02x the mean) held to it, giving 3.78 uL/min. IT DOES NOT APPLY TO THE PRE-QUENCH RINSE, and holding it there was ruining the experiment. contracts/parameters.json has carried shear.prelysis_rinse_ceiling_dyn_cm2 = 0.3 dyn/cm2 for exactly this case - half the published adherent-cell detachment onset of 0.6 dyn/cm2 (doi 10.1039/b820380f), applied for seconds to cells that are about to be deliberately killed - and nothing read it. The rinse now runs at 58.08 uL/min and takes about 18 s, against 1.93 uL/min and 580 s on the culture ceiling. ITS VOLUME IS SET BY THE EXCHANGE TARGET, NOT BY A ROUND NUMBER OF LANE VOLUMES: the rinse is a SWEEP (contracts/schemas/protocol.schema.json exchange_kind), so it needs -ln(1 - exchange.target_fraction) = 4.61 field volumes = 13.263 uL to reach 99%, plus the 4.189 uL of upstream dead volume that holds the same medium and must pass before anything clean reaches the field: 17.452 uL, 18.0 s. The bare contract floor alone would be 13.7 s. The quench flood and the solubilisation flush are sweeps too, at 1.3x and 1.9x that volume; the four elution chases are PARTIALS, because taking a defined fraction (field + downstream = 7.069 uL) is the point and sweeping one to 99% would dilute the metabolome about 2.5x and break the <=10 uL extract rule; the lane primes are FILLS, into a dry lane with nothing to clear. THE BIOLOGY AGREES AND THE REPO HAD IT BACKWARDS: Kapoore 2017 (doi 10.1039/C7AN00207F) found that WASHING ITSELF CAUSES metabolite leakage, so it is an argument for the SHORTEST defensible rinse, not for a careful slow one; it was previously cited here in favour of a long wash. Lorenz 2011 (doi 10.1021/ac103313x) is the paper that says rinse at all - a quick rinse roughly doubles detected features. Fast and brief satisfies both. The quench flood, chases and flush are held to no shear ceiling: the cells are dead. The combs are not culture: any cell there is not counted. VISCOSITY PROVENANCE, since shear goes as mu: the 37 C steps use contracts fluid.viscosity_37c_pa_s (0.8 mPa s, medium at 37 C); the rinse uses fluid.viscosity_pa_s (water at 20 C) carried to 4 C by the textbook water ratio (1.56 mPa s), because it is an aqueous buffer on ice and not medium; the cold organic solvent is neither and has no contract value, so 2.5 mPa s is an ASSUMPTION used only for flood pressure and Reynolds number. THERMAL ZONES, DECLARED AT LAST, INCLUDING THE SUB-AMBIENT ONE. This chip used to declare no thermal zones at all while its protocol demanded four setpoints, which meant tools/check_chip_spec.py's material and temperature checks never fired on it. One zone, tz_lane_fields, now covers all three fields from -20 C to 37 C: 37 C culture, 4 C rinse and flood, -20 C extraction soak, ambient (22 C) resolubilisation. ONE ZONE, NOT THREE, and that is a design finding, not a shortcut: three independently controlled -20/+37 C stages on 10 mm lane centres through a 0.5 mm COC base would fight each other, so one stage serves the whole board. CONSEQUENCES THE PROTOCOL NOW OBEYS: it cannot hold one lane at -20 C while the others are alive, so the protocol is ordered BY PHASE and not by lane; the stage must stay at 4 C through the quench floods and only go sub-ambient once every lane holds organic solvent, because ramping to -20 C with aqueous rinse buffer in a lane would FREEZE it - the slow freeze-quench this comb geometry exists to avoid; and the stage warms back to ambient BEFORE the aqueous solubilisation buffer goes in, for the same reason. The old lane-by-lane order broke all three. THE -20 C REQUIREMENT IS NEW TO THE RIG: protocols/thermal_map.md said 'no chiller, no water jacket', which was written before this module existed. That contradiction is resolved in thermal_map.md in favour of the rig needing a sub-ambient source, because the precipitated protein film is on this chamber's floor and cannot be moved off chip without losing the substrate for fraction 2. The soak is 300 s at -20 C (the published floor for a cold sequential extraction; the old 30 s at 4 C under-extracts and may not form that film at all). The Peltier also holds the collected extract cold, which improves ADP/ATP recovery by about 40-45% (doi 10.1007/s00216-019-02018-3). EXTRACT VOLUME IS THE DESIGN RULE. The lever for metabolomics is extract volume, not cell count. Each fraction is collected at 7.069 uL = the field plus everything downstream of it (outlet comb + stub), which is the honest definition of what reaches the vial. About 9600 cells (ASSUMED 1000/mm2 on 9.6 mm2) in 7.069 uL is about 1358 cells/uL, so a 2-5 uL injection is about 2716-6790 cell-equivalents. Keep the extract at or below about 10 uL. Do not grow field area if the extract grows in proportion: concentration then never improves, because field volume per cell is fixed by the 0.3 mm depth. Shrink spine width, teeth and stubs (the overhead) before adding area - and note that at target scale REPLICATING fields is how yield grows, which is another reason scale-up belongs in module1_target and not here. PORT ALLOCATION (6 of 6). in_n, out_n, in_g, out_g, in_a, out_a. Each inlet sits behind its OWN off-chip selector valve (cell suspension, culture medium, cold rinse, cold quench, solubilisation buffer: five positions). Each outlet sits behind its OWN off-chip fraction collector, a three-position valve: waste, vial M (metabolome), vial P (proteome). The SECOND collection is a second fraction out of the SAME port at a different time. HOW THE TWO FRACTIONS STAY APART: the valve is at waste for the rinse and the quench flood; it turns to vial M only for the extract chase; it returns to waste for the flush of 3 wetted volumes (33.774 uL) of solubilisation buffer, which clears the port hole, the stub and the lane of fraction 1; then it turns to vial P for the protein chase. Separate vials and separate valve ports mean fractions never share a vial. Nothing from one lane reaches another lane's valve, vial or line; only clean reagent reservoirs are shared upstream of the valves, each behind a check valve. A COLLECTION IS NOT INSTANT: the protocol's collect steps now carry real durations (two valve actuations, clearing the 1.003 uL outlet stub into the vial, then capping it and moving it to the cold block), where six of them used to declare 0.0 s for a physical fraction collection. CARRY-OVER RISK. Fraction 1 into fraction 2: after fraction 1 the stub holds about 1.0 uL of extract; the waste flush is many stub volumes, but the lane itself keeps at most exp(-3) = 5% of the old solvent and its metabolites under ideal mixing (a laminar slot displaces better; unmeasured, to be shown with a dye test). That residue adds a little organic solvent and small metabolites to fraction 2, which bottom-up proteomics tolerates. Fraction 2 into fraction 1: none, because 2 comes later. Precipitate fines can pass into fraction 1 if the flood strips the floor film (mean floor shear in the flood is about 5 dyn/cm2, hottest tooth about 10); spin vial M and add its pellet to fraction 2. Dead-end valve ports do not mix ideally, so every bound is a design bound, not a measurement. YIELD. Floor area 9.6 mm2 per lane; at an ASSUMED 1000 cells/mm2 (a dense monolayer; sparser lineages such as neurons may give 2-3x fewer) that is about 9600 cells per lane, 28800 for the chip. Proteomics is comfortable at this input: 1,000 cells already gives 500-1,000 proteins (Mueller 2020 doi 10.15252/msb.20199111), so about 10x headroom. Metabolomics: the old 1e5-1e6 cell figure describes conventional 2.1 mm-column workflows. On nanoflow HILIC or CE-MS, 100 cells gave 1,620 peak pairs (doi 10.1021/acs.analchem.7b03100); roughly 1e3 cells gives 40-100 identified metabolites, 1e4 gives 100-160, 1e5 gives 200-300; AMP/ADP/ATP are seen from 500 cells by CE-MS (doi 10.1016/j.jchromb.2018.12.004) - though see the rinse caveat above before believing an adenylate number from this chip. So about 1e4 cells is usable untargeted coverage of roughly 100-160 metabolites, provided the extract stays at or below about 10 uL. Medium: the lane holds 11.258 uL against about 0.019 uL of intracellular volume (ASSUMED 2 pL per cell), about 593:1, so the rinse is not optional: it is what makes medium-borne metabolites (amino acids, glucose) measurable; metabolites absent from medium (nucleotides, phosphorylated glycolytic intermediates) are unaffected. UNTESTED. Whether the teeth really convect into the rib shadows (load-bearing, see above); whether the flood strips the precipitated protein film; whether the field-only adhesion coat keeps the combs cell-free; tooth flow uniformity (model only); whether COC tolerates the quench and solubilisation reagents over the contact time (compatibility is still TODO in contracts/materials.json, and the PMMA coupon test named elsewhere in the repo is the wrong polymer for this chip); whether a single stage really reaches -20 C under a 0.5 mm COC base; the 0.4 mm ribs between teeth (the floor, with no margin). Untargeted metabolomics at this input needs the nanoflow or CE-MS platform, not a conventional column. Protocol: protocols/module6_v1.json, generated by protocols/build_module6.py - the JSON is not hand-edited any more. THERMAL ZONE DETAIL (the schema allows no note on a zone, so it lives here). ONE stage under all three fields, four setpoints in sequence: 37 C culture, 4 C pre-quench rinse and quench flood, -20 C extraction soak, ambient (22 C) resolubilisation. Deliberately one zone and not three: three independent -20/+37 C stages on 10 mm lane centres through a 0.5 mm COC base would fight each other. Consequence: the protocol is ordered BY PHASE, because one stage cannot hold one lane at -20 C while another is still alive at 37 C; the stage stays at 4 C through the floods so no lane is ever taken sub-ambient with aqueous buffer in it; and it returns to ambient before the aqueous solubilisation buffer goes in. min_temp_c is SUB-AMBIENT and the rig has no sub-ambient source today - see protocols/thermal_map.md, where that contradiction is resolved in favour of adding one. purpose is 'culture' because culture does happen here and that is the check worth firing; the extraction setpoints are in the same zone because they are the same piece of hardware. max_temp_c 37 C is far below COC's 120 C working limit, so the material check passes - it simply never ran before, because this chip declared no zones at all.

chambers.note: Neurons lane culture field for ADHERENT cells, 1.2 x 8 x 0.3 mm = 2.88 uL, floor area 9.6 mm2 (about 9600 cells at an ASSUMED 1000/mm2). No retention feature: the cells are attached to the floor. Fed from its left long edge by the inlet comb and drained at its right long edge by the outlet comb, so flow crosses the 1.2 mm short dimension. The quench, the cold soak and the protein resolubilisation all happen here, in place. VOLUME IS NOT THE LANE VOLUME: this chamber holds 2.88 uL and the lane around it holds 11.258 uL (4.189 upstream + 2.88 field + 4.189 downstream). Every exchange in the protocol is sized in LANE volumes because the combs and stubs are in series with the field; the LOAD is the one step capped at this chamber's own volume, which is what stops it over-declaring by 3.97x and what keeps cell suspension out of the outlet comb. In the one thermal zone tz_lane_fields.

channels.note: Neurons inlet comb: a 0.8 mm spine along the left long edge from the top-end port downwards, with 13 side teeth 0.2 x 1.5 mm at 0.6 mm pitch (0.4 mm ribs) opening into the field. Carries cell suspension, medium, rinse, quench and solubilisation buffer, one at a time. VOLUME 3.186 uL, DERIVED, not quoted: spine 8.4 x 0.8 x 0.3 mm = 2.016 uL plus 13 teeth of 0.2 x 1.5 x 0.3 mm = 1.170 uL. The tooth width is contracts/blocks.json min_open_channel_mm, the rib is min_wall_mm, the pitch is their sum, the count is the field's 8 mm edge divided by that pitch, and the tooth length is the spine-edge-to-field-edge gap these coordinates already state. protocols/build_module6.py recomputes all of it; the chip_spec schema has no volume field for a channel, which is the only reason this number is in a note. With the inlet stub (1.003 uL) this is the 4.189 uL of dead volume UPSTREAM of the field that the protocol's PRIME step pays for explicitly. During the quench flood this spine runs Re ~ 14 and its teeth Re ~ 2.4: inertial in the spine, near-creeping in the teeth, and the tooth branches are entrance-effect features. The 0.4 mm ribs cast 0.3-0.6 mm dead zones that diffusion alone would take 326-1303 s to clear, so tooth convection into those shadows is load-bearing and UNMEASURED.

Neurons outlet comb: 13 side teeth 0.2 x 1.5 mm offset half a pitch from the inlet teeth, gathering into a 0.8 mm spine that drains to the bottom-end port. Both fractions leave through it, at different times. VOLUME 3.186 uL, DERIVED, not quoted: spine 8.4 x 0.8 x 0.3 mm = 2.016 uL plus 13 teeth of 0.2 x 1.5 x 0.3 mm = 1.170 uL. With the outlet stub (1.003 uL) this is the 4.189 uL DOWNSTREAM of the field, and field + downstream = 7.069 uL is exactly what a chase pushes into a vial: the honest extract volume, and the number the <=10 uL design rule is tested against. It is deliberately never filled with cell suspension - the load stops at the far field edge - so cells cannot be stranded past the field.
